The analysis was done using the following five indicators:
1. Moving Averages 
2. MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence)
3. RSI (Relative Strength Index)
4. Fibonacci Retracement
5. Bollinger Bands

Moving Averages indicator measures the price point of a stock over a period of time. The results were very positive with a score of 10 indicating a high probability of the price increasing. 

MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) gives you insights into changes in the relationship between two moving averages. This method also gave a high positive score of 10.

RSI (Relative Strength Index) determines whether a stock is overbought or oversol, and it gave a score of 9 suggesting that the stock is not overbought.

Fibonacci Retracement is a method to identify the potential support and resistance levels in a price chart. The indicator gave a neutral score of 5.

Bollinger Bands is a volatility indicator that provides insights on when a stock is overbought or oversol. The indicator gave a very positive score of 9.

In summary, while not all the methods agree completely on the direction of the price, the majority of them suggest that the price will likely continue to go up, with a medium overall risk.

The fibonacci retracement and bollinger bands show no clear indication of a breakout or breakdown.
